text:
In Al-Adsani v. the United Kingdom (Grand Chamber, 21 November 2001), the European Court of Human Rights held that the United Kingdom did not breach the Convention by recognising Kuwait’s state immunity and thereby barring Al-Adsani’s civil claim for damages for alleged torture. It found no violation of Article 3 unanimously, and no violation of Article 6 § 1 by nine votes to eight, treating the immunity bar as a proportionate limit on access to a court that reflected a generally recognised rule of international law. It unanimously held that it was unnecessary to examine the Article 13 complaint separately.
CONFIDENCE: 90
